_what: Which of a person's passkeys may raise a ceiling or make another guarded change (src/passkey-authority.mjs; the ceilings are src/cap-change.json). The user-verification flag a passkey sends is reported by the authenticator itself and Trillion asks for no attestation (src/passkey-options.mjs), so a key pair a script makes can claim it, and a fresh sign-in (an emailed code, a password, a passkey link an AI made) is something an AI can hold. The wall is therefore custody of enrollment, not the flag. A passkey is KNOWN (has authority) from a moment fixed when it is saved, by its `provenance`: the passkey that made the account (sign-up) is known at once; one added in a ceremony opened with a confirmation from a known passkey, or vouched for by one (known-passkey), is known only after the notice row's hours and is told at once on every channel, so one deceived touch adds nothing at once and the person can remove it before then (removing a passkey that is not known needs only a recent sign-in). A passkey link always adds a passkey no known passkey confirmed: it is never vouched by the link itself. Only the operator account makes a link for another account, and only with a confirmation from the operator's own known passkey for exactly that account's link (passkeys/link-for); that account is told at once on every channel. A passkey added any other way waits out the notice (notice) ONLY on an account that has no known passkey, or while a recovery the person asked for is waiting (it is then known no sooner than the recovery ends); on an account that has a known passkey it signs in but never becomes known (unvouched), until a known passkey vouches for it. A recovery (an account whose known passkeys are lost) waits the notice row's hours, after which every passkey known before it started stops being known. Every passkey but the sign-up passkey, every recovery and every confirmation a known passkey makes (confirmed_*) is told at once on every way the person can be told (a service notice told on `every_channel`, which the person's choices cannot narrow, of kind `notice.kind`, opening `notice.open`; and the account's sign-in email, as mail kind `notice.mail_kind`), at most `notice.most` times in `notice.window_hours`, so floods cannot use up the mail the person is told by. Any use of a known passkey (signing in, confirming) cancels everything waiting that no known passkey confirmed: such a waiting passkey stops waiting and is never known, a waiting recovery ends. While anything waits, no way the person is told may be removed and no other sign-in may be ended. On an account with a known passkey, removing a way the person is told, ending another sign-in, disconnecting everything, deleting the account and removing a known passkey each need a confirmation from a known passkey bound to that exact change (src/cap-change.mjs holdCapConfirmation). A refusal for want of one names `step_needed` and the exact `change`, which a page answers by running the passkey confirmation for that change (src/passkey-step.mjs confirmWithPasskey) and sending the same request again. The wait is operator DATA here, never a person's setting, so no credential can shorten it. Remaining risk, stated: on an account with no known passkey, where an AI controls every way the person is told, nothing exists that only the person can do; whoever controls those ways gains authority after the notice. A passkey record with no provenance is never known. Passkeys saved before provenance existed are classified once, and only their provenance is written (src/passkey-authority.mjs legacyAuthority). Where a guard runs (the first time the account's authority is read) no evidence of sign-up is read: each is unvouched beside a passkey known with provenance, else it waits out the notice from then, so nobody is locked out (the person gets the notice path), and the person is told on every channel. The operator's one-time migration (src/passkey-provenance-migration.mjs, scripts/classify-legacy-passkeys.mjs) then reads the evidence: the account's sign-up passkey (the account was made with a passkey, src/profile-names.mjs sign-up record, and this one was saved at most `legacy.sign_up_seconds` before it) is known from its creation, and every other one is unvouched beside it, told again. On an account with no known passkey, deleting it or moving it into another account and retiring it waits out the notice row's hours (delayed_*): told at once on every channel, cancelled by a known passkey's use or any recent sign-in, and done only when the same change is asked again after the wait. On an account with a known passkey, moving it into another account needs a known passkey's confirmation for exactly that move, made in the account being moved. `confirm_words` is what the page shows while the passkey prompt for a confirmation is up, one row per change a confirmation may be for, filled from the change: the passkey prompt itself looks the same as a sign-in, so the words say exactly what the touch approves, and a confirmation is made only for a change named here.

words.not_known_yet: This passkey cannot confirm this change until {from}: it was added without a confirmation from a passkey you already had. Use a passkey you had before, or wait until then.
words.never_known: This passkey signs in, but it was added without a confirmation from a passkey you already had, so it cannot confirm changes. Vouch for it on Account & security with a passkey you had before.
words.needs_known_passkey: This change needs your passkey: confirm it with a passkey you already had.
words.held_while_waiting: A new passkey or a passkey recovery is waiting, so the ways you are told cannot change now. Remove the waiting passkey, cancel the recovery, or sign in with a passkey you had before, which cancels it.
words.too_many_notices: Too many passkeys were added or recoveries asked for on this account today. Try again tomorrow.
words.added_title: A new passkey was added to your Trillion account
words.added_body: It signs in now. From {from} it can also confirm changes to your limits. If you did not add it, remove it on Account & security before then, or sign in with a passkey you had before; either cancels it.
words.added_unvouched_body: It signs in, but it cannot confirm changes to your limits, since no passkey you had confirmed it. If you did not add it, remove it on Account & security.
words.recovery_title: Someone asked to recover the passkeys on your Trillion account
words.recovery_body: From {from} the passkeys you have now stop confirming changes to your limits. If you did not ask for this, sign in with one of them before then; that cancels it.
words.recovery_started: Recovery started. From {from} your old passkeys stop confirming changes, and a passkey you add now can confirm them from then.
words.recovery_not_needed: Your account has no passkey that confirms changes now, so a passkey you add waits out its notice without a recovery.
words.vouched: This passkey can confirm changes to your limits from {from}. Everywhere you are told hears of it now.
words.delayed_title: Someone asked to delete your Trillion account or move it away
words.delayed_body: It goes ahead only if it is asked again after {from}. If you did not ask for this, sign in with a passkey you had before, or cancel it on Account & security; either ends it.
words.delayed_started: This waits until {from}, and everywhere you are told hears of it now. Ask again after then to go ahead.
words.delayed_waiting: This waits until {from}. Ask again after then to go ahead.
words.delayed_other: Another change that deletes or moves your account is waiting until {from}. Cancel it first, or wait.
words.not_a_change: That is not a change a passkey confirms here.
words.added_vouched_body: It signs in now. A passkey you already had confirmed adding it, so from {from} it can also confirm changes to your limits. If you did not add it, remove it on Account & security before then.
words.confirmed_title: Your passkey confirmed a change on your Trillion account
words.confirmed_body: {words} If you did not do this, sign in with your passkey and undo it on Account & security or your Spend screen: a raised ceiling and a passkey added this way wait before they count.
words.legacy_unvouched_body: Passkeys on your account saved before Trillion recorded how each was added ({count}) still sign you in, but they confirm changes only once a passkey that already confirms changes vouches for them on Account & security.
words.legacy_waits_body: Passkeys on your account saved before Trillion recorded how each was added ({count}) still sign you in, and from {from} they can confirm changes again. If you do not recognize one, remove it on Account & security before then.
words.link_for_title: Trillion's operator made a link that adds a passkey to your account
words.link_for_body: Whoever opens it before {until} can add a passkey that signs in to your account; it cannot confirm changes to your limits unless a passkey you have vouches for it, and you will be told when it is added. If you did not ask for this, remove any passkey you do not recognize on Account & security.

confirm_words.cap: Confirm with your passkey: change a limit's ceiling, or what the limit covers or when it stops.
confirm_words.billing-month: Confirm with your passkey: start your billing month on day {cycle_day}.
confirm_words.paid-ceiling: Confirm with your passkey: set your paid ceiling to {dollars} dollars.
confirm_words.passkeys/new: Confirm with your passkey: add a new passkey that can confirm changes once its notice has passed.
confirm_words.passkeys/vouch: Confirm with your passkey: let another of your passkeys confirm changes once its notice has passed.
confirm_words.passkeys/remove: Confirm with your passkey: remove a passkey that confirms changes.
confirm_words.email/remove: Confirm with your passkey: remove your sign-in email.
confirm_words.email/replace: Confirm with your passkey: change your sign-in email to {email}.
confirm_words.phone/remove: Confirm with your passkey: remove phone sign-in.
confirm_words.password/remove: Confirm with your passkey: remove your password.
confirm_words.authenticator/remove: Confirm with your passkey: remove your authenticator app.
confirm_words.backup-codes/new: Confirm with your passkey: make new backup codes, which ends the old ones.
confirm_words.backup-codes/remove: Confirm with your passkey: remove your backup codes.
confirm_words.sessions/end: Confirm with your passkey: sign out another browser.
confirm_words.account/disconnect: Confirm with your passkey: disconnect every key, app and computer.
confirm_words.account/delete: Confirm with your passkey: delete your Trillion account and everything in it.
confirm_words.account/move: Confirm with your passkey: move everything in this account into another account ({to}).
confirm_words.passkeys/link-for: Confirm with your passkey: make a link that adds a passkey to the account {account}, which that account is told of.
